short: The prison beneath the lead roof of Venice’s Doge’s Palace.
note: The “Leads”: prison cells beneath the lead-covered roof of the Doge’s Palace in Venice. Giacomo Casanova was imprisoned there and escaped in 1756.

short: Giacomo Casanova, Venetian adventurer and memoirist.
note: Giacomo Casanova (1725–1798), Venetian adventurer and memoirist, famous for his love affairs and his escape from the Piombi prison in 1756.

short: Possibly Greek hylē: matter or material.
note: Possibly Greek hylē (ὕλη), originally wood or timber and, in philosophy, the matter or material from which something is made.

short: Illusion or the world of appearances in Indian philosophy.
note: In Vedanta, the manifold world perceived by the senses insofar as it conceals the unity of absolute being; more broadly, illusion.

short: William Hogarth, the English painter and engraver.
note: William Hogarth (1697–1764), English painter and engraver known for satirical sequences of modern life, including A Rake’s Progress and Marriage A-la-Mode.
Decoratively painted, enameled, or lacquered sheet-metal ware, often associated with eighteenth-century household objects.

short: Possibly an echo of Hamlet’s first soliloquy.
note: Possibly an echo of Hamlet, act 1, scene 2, where Shakespeare’s prince wishes that his solid flesh could dissolve.
